subject: CAIQ runtime controls crosswalk & KV-cache log handoff
messages:
From: Audits Team <audits@nebulahealth.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ runtime control evidence request - KV cache and model access logs

Monica —

Thanks again for taking time on Friday. As part of our CSA/CAIQ assessment we need to validate runtime controls around model access, KV/prefix caching, and request-level auditability. Specifically Nebula needs: 

- A control crosswalk that maps Redwood runtime behaviors (e.g., KV cache eviction, prefix caching, model-variant fallback) to CAIQ/CSA control IDs. We prefer a single spreadsheet mapping control ID -> your statement -> evidence artifact.
- A sample of runtime logs that show per-request model selection and cache hits/misses (sanitized is fine; we only need structure and a short sample of rows).
- A short README explaining retention policy, redaction approach, and how logs tie to the controls.

Target timeline is COB next week (2027-08-06) to keep the audit window moving. Please let me know if that's feasible or if you need an extension.

Best,
Lara Kim
Security & Compliance, Nebula Health

[This message may be subject to NDA rules between parties]

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Audits Team <audits@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ runtime control evidence request - KV cache and model access logs

Hi Lara —

Thanks — we can provide exactly the artifacts you listed. Plan below: 

1) Crosswalk spreadsheet mapping CSA/CAIQ control IDs -> Redwood control statement -> evidence filename. I'll attach the working copy. (See caiq_crosswalk_runtime_controls.xlsx)
2) Sanitized sample log export showing request_id, timestamp, model_variant, cache_hit (true/false), kv_cache_key, action, and truncated payload hashes. We'll provide a 1,000-row sample as runtime_kv_cache_log_sample.csv.
3) README (audit_readme.txt) that outlines log retention (90 days for detailed traces, 365 days aggregated), redaction rules (PII removed at ingestion using hashing), and where the canonical logs live in our secure S3 bucket plus the internal runbook/Playbook link.

Karthik will include the mapping of control rationales and evidence locations; Michael will follow up if we need to extract a narrower timeframe or additional indices. Are you okay with us delivering a single ZIP with the three items by EOD 2027-08-04?

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: caiq_crosswalk_runtime_controls.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Audits Team <audits@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ runtime control evidence request - KV cache and model access logs

Lara / Monica —

Adding a few clarifications from the security side to make the crosswalk audit-ready: 

- Control mapping: in the spreadsheet each row will include the CSA control ID (e.g., CCM-DA-02 / IAM-01 equivalencies), our formal control statement, a short implementation note (e.g., "model-variant routing enforced by policy X, enforced in control-plane service rp-router-v2"), and the evidence filename + path.
- Logs: the sample will be redacted such that customer prompt/response text is replaced with SHA256 hashes; session identifiers are preserved. We will also include an example of how a cache miss triggers a model-variant fallback (fields: cache_hit=false, fallback_variant=m-lite-1q8, latency_ms). 
- Retention & access: canonical raw traces are stored in an encrypted S3 path with KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 (we will not share the key, only evidence that the key policy is restricted). Note: I included a short pointer to our internal runbook in the README (Drive link).

If Nebula needs longer-term retention evidence (beyond 365 days) or an export covering production traffic for a specific date range, we can produce a separate request but it will need a formal request and approval (SEC-719). For the current CAIQ submission the sample + crosswalk should suffice.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: audit_readme.txt (contains retention policies and runbook link)

Monica / Karthik —

Received, thanks for the quick turnaround. The plan and artifacts look good at a high level. Two small asks before we close this control: 

1) In the crosswalk, can you add an explicit row for "control evidence: example log row mapping to control statement" (i.e., link the sample CSV row number to the control ID) so our assessors can trace a concrete example?
2) In the README, please include the S3 object prefix pattern (not the KMS key) that we can reference in the submission (e.g., s3://redwood-prod-logs/runtime/yyyy-mm-dd/).

If you can add those items in the ZIP by EOD Friday (2027-08-06) we'll consider this control addressed and proceed to the next CAIQ section.

Best,
Lara Kim
Security & Compliance, Nebula Health
